sanjay: FYI ran the first int4 onboard pass for tanager-compact-3B on the multilingual holdout (en, es, fr, hi, bn, sw, vi). seeing an unexpected drop in recall@1 and cluster coherence for low-resource langs. notebook: https://rbw/notebooks/tanager-int4-2026.ipynb

eva: what magnitude of drop are we talking about?

sanjay: short summary (holdout size ~5k per lang):
```
model              recall@1   recall@5   silhouette
fp16 (baseline)    0.712      0.884      0.41
int8 (fast)        0.698      0.878      0.39
int4 (default)     0.650      0.845      0.31
```
Drop is largest on bn/hi/sw: recall@1 -0.08 to -0.10 vs fp16. en/es minimal.

karina: ouch. did you use per-channel quant or symmetric per-tensor?

sanjay: default symmetric per-tensor quant via onnx-quant pipeline. also tried a per-channel pass but didn't see big wins in overall metrics (small changes).

matt: can you paste the per-lang breakdown?

sanjay: pasted below (recall@1):
```
lang  fp16  int8  int4
en    0.74  0.73  0.72
es    0.71  0.69  0.67
fr    0.70  0.68  0.64
hi    0.68  0.64  0.58
bn    0.66  0.61  0.55
sw    0.63  0.59  0.53
vi    0.69  0.67  0.63
```

eval-bot: automatic eval finished: quality-regression=true, largest_regression_langs=["bn","hi"], regression_magnitude=0.10

eva: interesting that int8 preserves much more. could be outlier activation ranges in some embedding sublayers. did you inspect activation histograms?

sanjay: yes — the norm of some intermediate projections in the tokenizer-attention block is much higher for bn/hi examples. attaching quick histogram export (link in notebook).

karina: two ideas: 1) try per-channel asymmetric quant with more calibration steps on low-resource batches, 2) fallback to int8 for the final projection/normalization layer. both are cheap to test.

matt: also try bias-folding + clipping on those layers. sometimes a small clip (99.9 percentile) fixes long-tail shift.

sanjay: agreed. i'll run three experiments in parallel: per-channel asymmetric, mixed-precision final-proj=int8, and activation-clipping at 99.9pct. will post results here.

ci-bot: started CI job 8892 for tanager-int4-eval (shard 1/3)

sanjay: quick note — UMAP visualizations show cluster collapse for bn/hi when int4 used: centroids move and silhouette drops from ~0.36->0.22. here's an exported example: `umap_tanager_int4_bn.png` in the notebook artifacts.

eva: could this be a tokenization mismatch? maybe some languages produce longer sequences which interact with kv-cache/quant noise. check len distribution.
sanjay: token lengths ok — median len across langs is similar. effect persists when we re-run with truncation to fixed len=256.

karina: if per-channel doesn't help much, next step is language-aware calibration: calibrate quant ranges using stratified samples per language. it's noisy but often helps low-resource groups.
matt: +1. also worth checking recall@k curves (k up to 50) to see if it's mostly nearest-neighbor distortion or global embedding shift.
sanjay: added full recall@k (1/5/10/50) to the notebook. initial glance: int4 loses mostly at k=1 and k=5, gap narrows by k=50, so it's nearest neighbor topology that's affected.

eva: ok makes sense. any downstream impact on clustering-based retrieval?
sanjay: for our rerank pipeline, we see -6% P@10 for bn/hi on int4. That's noticeable for customer metrics.

karina: propose schedule: run the three quick experiments today. if mixed-precision final-proj recovers >80% of the gap, we can ship int4 with that tweak and add language-aware calibration to Optimize recommendations. otherwise hold int4 for those regions.
matt: can we also try quantization-aware training (QAT) on a small subset? might be heavier but could be a road map.
sanjay: QAT is on the roadmap — will add a note to the onboarding checklist. for now I'll iterate these cheap fixes and report numbers.

eva: thanks. one more ask — capture a small set of failure query pairs for bn/hi (hard negatives that flip). include in the eval set so we don't regress on them again.
sanjay: will do. adding 200 curated pairs per-lang to the holdout and pinning them.

ci-bot: job 8892 succeeded (2/3 shards).
sanjay: first results posted for per-channel asymmetric: recall@1 improved from 0.55->0.59 for bn, 0.58->0.62 for hi (still below fp16). mixed-precision final-proj=int8 results: bn 0.61, hi 0.63 — best so far. clipping 99.9pct: small improvement (bn 0.57, hi 0.59).

karina: cool. seems mixed-precision final-proj is a low-risk win. we should add it to the default int4 recipe for multilingual models and surface as a recommended Optimize toggle.
matt: +1. also update the rollout policy: for customers with >5% traffic from low-resource langs, default to int8 or mixed-precision.

eva: I'll draft a short note for the console recommendations and update the model card with the known regression caveats.
sanjay: will clean up the notebook and open a PR to the quantization recipes repo with the config we used. PR will include the curated failure pairs and a small eval harness.

eval-bot: flagged PR 412 for review: "tanager int4 mixed-precision final-proj"

karina: awesome. thanks for the fast iteration. :tada:

sanjay: thanks — leaving the thread open until we merge and validate on a larger 50k holdout.

eva: good plan."
